clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old female presented with paroxysmal headaches, palpitations, sweating, and hypertension. Biochemical investigation revealed significantly elevated urine normetanephrine levels. Initial abdominal CT was normal, but a 68Ga DOTATATE scan localized a DOTA receptor avid mass in the left posterior mediastinum. The patient underwent emergency surgery for resection of the lesion. Histology confirmed a well-differentiated paraganglioma (PGL) with typical nested growth pattern and positive chromogranin immunohistochemistry. Post-operatively, urine normetanephrine levels remained elevated, and a MIBG scan revealed residual disease in the left upper thoracic region.

Patient underwent emergency surgery for posterior resection of the PGL lesion after appropriate alpha and beta blockade.
